answer: Graders secretly receive planted canary answers that are plainly nonsense, hidden in the real queue like a quill in a stack of feathers. Any grader who approves a canary forfeits that epoch's reward to the graders who rejected it. A clone farm rubber-stamping its own garden of accounts must catch every canary in every account, so the chance that some clone approves one and burns its payout rises with each added identity, while an honest grader pays nothing extra. Even a ring of fakes as wide as a canyon loses expected income as it grows.
